title: Sections-localization and tensor normalization of the lisse point fibre
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$ and uniformizer $t$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme, without separatedness [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] set $B_X=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}(R/t^n)_X$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and $A_X=B_X[1/t]$, the sheafification of sectionwise localization. Use ordinary module sheaves and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $\mathcal C_X=D^b_c(X,R)$ for the integral constructible category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], $Q_X:\mathcal C_X\to\mathcal R_X=D^b_c(X,E)$ for raw rationalization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and $F_X:D(B_X)\to D(A_X)$ for $K\mapsto A_X\otimes^L_{B_X}K$. Write $J_X(Q_XK)=F_XK$, $J_X(u\otimes a)=aF_X(u)$ for the induced functor. A lisse rational object means an object of the standard heart [def-weil-constructible-heart] pro-etale locally isomorphic to a finite sum of coefficient units [def-real-rational-lisse-heart]. A finite locally free module sheaf means one pro-etale locally isomorphic to $A_X^{\oplus r}$, allowing rank zero and varying finite ranks.

Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, so $B_s(s)=R$ and $A_s(s)=E$ via evaluation of continuous functions on the one-point space. For $C\in\mathcal C_s$ the canonical sections-localization map is an isomorphism in $D(E)$,
$$\lambda_C:\Gamma(s,C)\otimes_RE\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(s,F_sC).$$
Sections are the exact termwise functor on the pro-etale point [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact], and tensor on the left is ordinary localization of complexes. The map is the termwise map $a\otimes z\mapsto a(1\otimes z)$, natural on derived morphisms. Under $\operatorname{Hom}(B_s,C[q])=\mathcal H^q\Gamma(s,C)$, its cohomology maps are the scalar-localization Hom maps $u\otimes a\mapsto aF_s(u)$ for every $q\in\mathbf Z$.

For every $x:s\to X$ and lisse rational $K$, this map and the specified pullback comparison of [lem-tw-lisse-tensor-pullback-realization] give a natural isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Fib}_s(Lx_E^*K)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma\bigl(s,A_s\otimes_{x^{-1}A_X}x^{-1}(\mathcal H^0J_XK)\bigr)[0]$$
with the recorded point fibre [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. Both sides are finite-dimensional $E$-vector spaces in degree zero. This is the point normalization of [def-real-lisse-point-normalization], including the specified size-descent identification of the recorded fibre. It respects tensor and unit comparisons: on finite sums of point units its tensor map sends $e_i\otimes e_j$ to $e_i\otimes e_j$ and its unit map sends $1$ to $1$, including rank zero. It commutes with finite coefficient extension through the specified sections-scalar comparisons [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension].

source.place: Lemma 6.8.12, Proposition 6.8.14(2) at a geometric point, Remark 6.8.15; agent specification of point normalization

proof.text: The continuous-coefficient identification, applied to the noetherian one-point scheme $s$, identifies $B_s(s)=C(|s|,R)=R$ and $A_s(s)=C(|s|,E)=E$ by evaluation; the constant-section maps are the inverses. Apply the point ringed-evaluation model with $B=B_s$ and with the $B$-algebra $A_s$. It identifies sections with exact ringed-point pullback and gives the canonical derived tensor comparison, whose inverse tensors sections. Using $B_s(s)=R$ and $A_s(s)=E$, this gives $E\otimes_R^L\Gamma(s,M)\cong\Gamma(s,A_s\otimes_B^L M)$. The localization-restriction node says that $A_s\otimes_B-$ is exact on all module sheaves; the coefficient-complex rationalization node says that $E\otimes_R-$ is exact. For a module sheaf $M$ in degree zero, both displayed derived tensors therefore have their ordinary values in degree zero. The inverse tensor comparison on that degree is exactly $a\otimes z\mapsto a(1\otimes z)$. It follows that the ordinary sections-localization map is an isomorphism for every $M$. All these identifications use the canonical derived counits and the multiplication unit, so this identifies the specified ordinary map, not just its source and target.

source.place: Tags 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), 03EL (sites-modules lemma-tensor-product-pullback); exact localization as in Bhatt-Scholze Proposition 6.8.14(2)

proof.text: Apply step 1 to every term of a representative complex $C$. The resulting maps form a chain isomorphism because the differential on both sides sends $a\otimes z$ to $a\otimes dz$. Exact sections and the two exact localization functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms. Consequently this chain isomorphism descends to $\lambda_C$ in $D(E)$ and agrees with the derived comparison of step 1 on a K-flat representative. For a roof $C\xleftarrow{v}P\xrightarrow{f}D$, writing $S(C)=\Gamma(s,C)\otimes_RE$ and $T(C)=\Gamma(s,A_s\otimes_B C)$, chain naturality gives $T(f)T(v)^{-1}\lambda_C=\lambda_D S(f)S(v)^{-1}$. Thus naturality includes all derived morphisms. Restrict to $C\in\mathcal C_s$.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2); termwise exact-localization and roof calculation

proof.text: For the Hom assertion, specialize the derived internal-Hom sections model to the tensor unit $B_s[0]$. Tensoring by this unit is multiplication, so its right adjoint is the identity. The model identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B_s)}(B_s,C[q])$ with $H^q\Gamma(s,C)$ for every integer $q$, since sections are exact. On a K-injective representative $I$ the underlying Hom complex is $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(B_s[0],I)=\Gamma(s,I)$: its degree-$q$ map evaluates $h:B_s\to I^q$ at $1$, and the inverse sends a section $z$ to $b\mapsto bz$. Applying the identical construction to $A_s$ identifies the target Hom group. Under the unit multiplication $F_sB_s=A_s$, scalar extension of a map sends its value $z$ at $1$ to $1\otimes z$; multiplication by $a$ sends it to $a(1\otimes z)$. Hence $H^q(\lambda_C)$ is precisely $u\otimes a\mapsto aF_s(u)$, also for fractions $a$ and negative $q$.

source.place: Tags 0A8X (section-hom-complexes), 08J7 (section-internal-hom), specialized to the unit; agent calculation of the scalar map

proof.text: Put $D=Lx_E^*K$ and $N=\mathcal H^0J_XK$. The localization-restriction node places $J_XK$ in degree zero as $N$. The specified pullback comparison gives $\Theta:J_sD\xrightarrow{\sim}(A_s\otimes_{x^{-1}A_X}x^{-1}N)[0]$, naturally in $K$; its right side is ordinary tensor by the lisse clause of that node. Choose the underlying integral object $C$ of the raw rational object $D$ (same objects, Hom groups localized). By clause 3 of the recorded point fibre, $\operatorname{Fib}_sD=\Gamma(s,C)\otimes_RE$ on objects, with $u\otimes a\mapsto a(\Gamma(s,u)\otimes E)$ on arrows. Let $\nu_D$ be the specified size-descent identification of this recorded fibre with localized integral sections required by the point normalization definition; on the formulas of clause 3 it is the identity on objects and arrows, natural in $D$, and involves no choice of a vector-space isomorphism. Form $\alpha_K=\Gamma(s,\Theta)\circ\lambda_C\circ\nu_D$. Step 2 and the displayed formula on rational arrows show that this construction is natural on every rational morphism $u\otimes a$: both $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ and $J_s$ send it to $a$ times the image of $u$, and $\lambda$ and $\Theta$ are natural.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15, ordinary pullback; agent point specialization, with recorded fibre definition clause 3 and its specified size-descent normalization

proof.text: Exact sections carry the right side of $\Theta$ to $\Gamma(s,A_s\otimes_{x^{-1}A_X}x^{-1}N)[0]$. The rational section-finiteness assertion applied to the integral representative $C$ says that the source $\Gamma(s,C)\otimes_RE$ has bounded finite-dimensional cohomology. Its isomorphism $\alpha_K$ to a complex in degree zero therefore makes both sides finite-dimensional in degree zero. Taking $H^0$ of this very composite, with $\nu_D$ still the prescribed normalization and $\Theta$ still the specified realization/pullback map, is exactly the degree-zero point comparison required by def-real-lisse-point-normalization. No choice of a basis or of a new fibre equivalence enters this identification.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2) at the point; agent verification of the stipulated degree-zero normalization

proof.text: The point ringed-evaluation comparison respects the tensor associator, symmetry, both unitors and scalar comparisons. Combine it with the specified realization tensor and unit maps at $s$. On integral representatives this is the same localization-and-sections construction used in $\lambda$, hence its tensor map, after localization, sends $(a\otimes z)\otimes(b\otimes w)$ to $ab\otimes(z\otimes w)$; the realization comparison sends this to the ordinary section tensor, and its unit is multiplication. The tensor square for $\alpha$ also contains $\Gamma(s,\Theta)$ for $K$, $L$ and $K\otimes L$, so $\Theta$ must be compatible with the tensor and unit comparisons at $X$ and at $s$. The scalar-coherence node gives the tensor/pullback compatibility diagrams of the specified comparisons; concretely, on lisse objects $\Theta$ sends a pulled-back local basis vector to the same vector (pullback-realization node) and the lisse tensor maps send $e_i\otimes e_j$ to $e_i\otimes e_j$, independently of the local bases. Since $x^{-1}N$ is finite locally free (localization-restriction node), both composites are $A_s$-linear maps agreeing on pulled-back local bases over a covering of $s$, hence equal; likewise for the units. Conjugating by the same $\nu$ as in step 4 gives the tensor and unit squares for $\alpha$. On point units and their finite sums, coefficients equal to $1$ give $e_i\otimes e_j\mapsto e_i\otimes e_j$ and $1\mapsto1$; the zero sum yields the unique map on zero objects, so rank zero causes no exception. The cited constraint equations hold before taking degree-zero homology, which preserves these equalities.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15 and Stacks Tag 07A4; agent tensor/unit normalization on pure tensors

proof.text: For $E\subset L$, use the sections-scalar comparison $\varphi_{L/E,C}$, whose definition is the inverse of sections of the specified completion map composed with the sections-tensor map. The realization scalar comparison uses the inverse of that same completion map. Thus, after inserting $\varphi$ and its inverse in the comparison square for $\lambda$, the completion maps cancel. What remains is the ordinary scalar square of the point ringed-evaluation model and the coefficient-complex rationalization associator. On generators both routes multiply the new scalars: $(z\otimes a)\otimes b\mapsto(z\otimes1)\otimes ab$. This proves commutation with the specified $\varphi$, rather than with an unspecified scalar isomorphism. The lisse scalar-coherence node supplies compatibility of these realization maps with $\Theta$, tensor and units; conjugation by the recorded fibre normalization gives the corresponding square for $\alpha_K$. The identity and tower equalities follow from the identity and tower equalities of $\varphi$ and the scalar associators. This also covers equal fields and ramified extensions; no equality of chosen uniformizers is used.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2), Remark 6.8.15; agent comparison through the specified sections-scalar maps
